 Kasparas Jakučionis 
 MIL 
 Guard 
 #25 
 Player Stats
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 Kasparas Jakučionis tallied a career-high 25 points (9-of-16 FGs, 4-of-10 FTs), five rebounds, five assists and three steals in 26 minutes off the bench in Sunday’s loss to the Hawks.
 Jakučionis took advantage of his opportunity with Ryan Rollins out with an illness, hoisting a season-high 16 shot attempts and going 4-of-10 from three-point range. He’s played sparingly in his Bucks debut, but he’s shown that he can heat up and score in bunches when he’s given a chance. His role figures to expand once the Bucks begin to jettison some of their veteran pieces around midseason. Milwaukee has a three-game week on tap with matchups against the Heat, Trail Blazers and 76ers.
 -  George Bissell

 Ryan Rollins 
 MIL 
 Guard 
 #13 
 Ryan Rollins amassed 14 points (5-of-9 FGs), five rebounds, two assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Knicks. 
 The Bucks didn’t have Tyler Herro for Tuesday’s game, so Rollins made his first start since Halloween. While the production was solid, he logged 24 minutes, with Kasparas Jakučionis (11 points, four assists, one steal and two three-pointers) playing 23 minutes off the bench. If Herro remains out for Wednesday’s game against the Lakers, Rollins may still have some value in 12-team leagues. That said, his recent move to the bench and reduced minutes are a major concern for managers who selected Rollins with a middle-round pick. 
 Kasparas Jakučionis 
 MIL 
 Guard 
 #25 
 Kasparas Jakucionis with 15 points (4-of-7 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, a block, and a three in 26 minutes. 
 He was one of the first players off the bench for the Bucks. Had a tough first half but got better in the second half. He still ended up with five fouls in this game. He likely won’t impact many fantasy leagues this year but in dynasty leagues, it will be something we continue to watch since the Bucks don’t have a surefire star on their roster. 
 Kasparas Jakučionis 
 MIL 
 Guard 
 #25 
 Kasparas Jakučionis tallied 18 points (3-of-8 FGs, 11-of-11 FTs), one rebound, six assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s exhibition against the Bulls. 
 Shipped to Milwaukee after one season as part of the Giannis Antetokounmpo trade, Jakučionis started Wednesday because the Bucks held out Ryan Rollins, Tyler Herro and Kevin Porter Jr. The second-year guard had his moments, leading the Bucks in assists and making 11 free throws. However, Jakučionis also committed five turnovers, which isn’t surprising for a young guard who played limited minutes as a rookie. Given Milwaukee’s perimeter depth, Jakučionis may struggle to earn consistent minutes this season. While that makes him a non-factor in redraft leagues, he should be rostered in dynasty leagues. 
 Kasparas Jakučionis 
 MIL 
 Guard 
 Kasparas Jakučionis recorded 11 points (2-of-10 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), three rebounds, six assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Heat. 
 The Bucks viewed Jakučionis as a key player in their negotiations with the Heat over Giannis Antetokounmpo, so it’s safe to assume they’ll do everything they can to make the second-year guard a key contributor next season. In his unofficial Bucks debut, the 6-foot-6 guard shot 0-of-7 from inside the arc. The good news was that Jakučionis did a good job of setting up teammates, and he shot 2-of-3 from beyond the arc. While he isn’t a lock to be fantasy-relevant next season, Jakučionis is worth keeping an eye on. 
 Kasparas Jakučionis 
 MIL 
 Guard 
 The Athletic’s Sam Amick reports the Bucks pushed for Kasparas Jakučionis to be included in the trade for Giannis Antetokounmpo. 
 Amick, citing league sources, reports the Heat initially attempted to include Davion Mitchell in the trade rather than Jakučionis. With Mitchell on an expiring contract, the Bucks wanted a player with more time remaining on their rookie contract. It was a reasonable ask considering two of the other players the Bucks acquired (Tyler Herro and Jaimie Jaquez Jr.) are also on expiring deals. The Bucks held out and landed Jakučionis, who has three years left on his contract. He remains an intriguing dynasty asset on the rebuilding Bucks. 
 Kasparas Jakučionis 
 MIL 
 Guard 
 #25 
 The Bucks have reportedly acquired Kasparas Jakučionis, Tyler Herro, Kel’el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr. and multiple picks from the Heat for Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bobby Portis. 
 Miami lead executive Pat Riley has reportedly landed his most recent “big fish,” and Jakučionis is among the players headed in the other direction. The 20th overall pick in the 2025 draft, the former Illinois standout averaged 6.2 points, 2.6 rebounds, 2.6 assists and 1.2 three-pointers in 53 appearances as a rookie. Shooting 42.9 percent from the field and 87.9 percent from the foul line, injuries led to Jakučionis making 12 starts. With Milwaukee clearly on a rebuilding path, the 6-foot-6 guard is worth keeping an eye on in redraft leagues, but he is not a “must-draft” player yet. However, Jakučionis’ ceiling in dynasty leagues has been raised with the reported trade. 
 Tyler Herro 
 MIA 
 Guard 
 #14 
 Tyler Herro (foot) and Davion Mitchell (shoulder) are available for Sunday’s game against the Hawks. 
 Herro and Mitchell are available for Sunday’s regular-season finale after not playing in Friday’s win over the Wizards. Their returns will push Simone Fontecchio and Kasparas Jakučionis to the bench, with the former offering a higher ceiling when used in a reserve role. A win over the Hawks, combined with a Hornets loss to the Knicks, would move Miami into the No. 9 seed. They would host the 9 vs. 10 game on Wednesday night.

 In his final game of Week 4, Gilgeous-Alexander did whatever he wanted against the Kings. Oklahoma City’s blowout win meant Gilgeous-Alexander got some additional rest, as he did not play in the fourth quarter.
